boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Crater record (July 30, 1864) in the Richmond-Petersburg Campaign [June 1864-March 1865]. Deep Bottom I (VA069) ends on July 29. Army-wide returns, raid-wide and multi-action loss totals, and the siege as a whole are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force field reads 'IX Corps [US]; elements of the Army of Northern Virginia [CS]' and the live field zero. Humphreys gives the Army of the Potomac 37,984 effective infantry on July 20 and the Army of Northern Virginia 39,295 on July 10 (excluding detached corps), with only Hoke's, Johnson's and Mahone's divisions left in the Petersburg lines. Burnside says his corps had been recruited from under 6,000 veterans to 24,000 men.
claims.rationale: Army-wide returns of other dates and a corps recruitment total; not the forces engaged at the crater. None is adopted as a matched opening strength; live zeros are not measured absence.

claims.value: Burnside says his plan to lead with the colored division was not adopted and that peremptory orders sent that division in; Humphreys says Ledlie did not accompany his division, that Burnside alone did not carry out his preparatory orders, that Lee ordered two of Mahone's brigades up, and that the assault failed from mismanagement and misbehavior of several chief actors. Meade told Burnside on August 3 that he had asked for his relief. The frozen commanders are Major General Burnside (US) and General Lee (CS); the live page gives Lee as Major General.
claims.rationale: Direction and blame are attributed as stated; Burnside's and Meade's accounts are adversarial and the Court of Inquiry record was not inspected. The live rank is not adopted. No listed commander receives automatic sole credit.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads 5,300 total and the live field 5,289 (US 3,798; CS 1,491). Humphreys gives Meade's report of 4,400 Union killed, wounded and missing, the Medical Department table's 4,008, his own estimate of probably 3,500, the colored division's 176 killed, 688 wounded and 801 missing, the table's Confederate 400, 600 and 200 (which he calls erroneous), McMaster's 677 for Elliott's brigade, and Mahone's 1,101 prisoners; Burnside's epoch table gives the Fourth Division 170 killed, 688 wounded and 801 missing.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. Burnside's and Humphreys' Fourth Division killed differ (170 against 176).

open_questions: The Court of Inquiry record (No. 4), Meade's August 16 report (read, not selected), Ledlie's, Potter's, Willcox's and Ferrero's reports, Ord's report, Lee's July 30 dispatches (read, not selected), Mahone's colors list and Confederate returns remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC (the live NPS page and the frozen Arnold rows) is one family. Humphreys' The Virginia Campaign of ’64 and ’65 (1883) is an interested history by the Army of the Potomac's chief of staff, later commander of its Second Corps, in the same author family as the registered From Gettysburg to the Rapidan; it relies on Meade's, Hancock's, Warren's, Burnside's, Parke's and Wilson's reports and quotes Lee's, Beauregard's and Gordon's despatches, so it is not independent of those families. Gillmore's, Meade's, Hancock's, Burnside's, Wilson's, Hampton's, Stannard's and Lee's papers, printed in Official Records Series I, Volumes XXXVI (Part 2), XL, XLII and XLVI (Part 1), are separate families of interested commanders' accounts; each volume is a shared container, not an additional witness. Lee's telegrams largely relay subordinates' reports. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
